label: Tyrol Grey

names.text: Alternative names as listed on the Wikipedia page (fetched).

about.text: An Alpine dual-purpose cattle breed of Tyrol in Austria and South Tyrol in Italy. Its milk is described as suitable for drinking and for cheese, butter and yogurt, and it is also kept for beef. The Wikipedia page describes its milk and beef performance as very good.

sources.text: Fetched page for the dual-purpose use and the 'very good' milk and beef performance. The drinking and cheese, butter and yogurt uses come from the WebSearch text of the same page, not from a separate fetch.
Place as stated on the fetched page. The page gives no formation dates, so none are recorded.
About 4,836 kg per cow per year in South Tyrol in 2002, from 8,491 control cows, as stated on the fetched page. No lactation figures are given.
Fat 3.78% and protein 3.38%, South Tyrol, 2002, as stated on the fetched page.
Described on the fetched page as dual-purpose, for milk and beef.

facts.v: Described as having the best milk amount-to-quality ratio among Italian mountain cattle breeds.

sources.text: Claim as stated on the fetched page.

facts.v: Good forage instinct and feed conversion, robust, long-lived and very fertile; breeding goals include hardiness, mountain pasture ability and easy calving.

sources.text: Traits as stated on the fetched page.

gaps: Looked for a current population count, a DAD-IS risk status, lactation length and a per-lactation yield. The only population figure seen was about 5,000 herdbook cows from an undated Austrian WebSearch snippet, which I did not open, so it is left out. The 2002 yield is the only yield figure found.
